South Dakota statutes set the basic rules between landlords and tenants, including deposits, notices and what happens when a rental is sold.

What the official sources say

  • Residential security deposit may not exceed one month's rent, except a larger deposit may be agreed where special conditions pose a danger to maintenance of the premises. (SDCL 43-32-6.1; source)
  • Landlord must return the deposit or give a written statement of specific reasons for withholding within 21 days after termination of tenancy and receipt of tenant's mailing address or delivery instructions; itemized accounting within 45 days on tenant request; failure forfeits right to withhold; bad-faith retention carries punitive damages up to $200. (SDCL 43-32-24; source)
  • Landlord must give reasonable notice of intent to enter; 24 hours' written notice is presumed reasonable unless the lease agrees otherwise; except emergencies or where impracticable. Notice states date(s), a period during normal business hours, and purpose. (SDCL 43-32-ent (Reasonable notice of landlord's intent to enter; section number not shown on fetched page); source)
  • In month-to-month leases the landlord may modify terms (including rent) by written notice at least 30 days before the end of the month; the tenant may terminate effective the first day of the next month by notice within 15 days of receiving the modification notice. (SDCL 43-32-15 (catchline: Modification of lease--Written notice by landlord; section number not displayed on fetched page); source)
  • Failure of the lessor to renew a written lease before or on expiration is not retaliation; lessee has remedies of 43-32-6 for retaliatory conduct. (SDCL 43-32-27, 43-32-28; source)
  • SD Consumer Protection: tenant should give notice to end lease at least one full rental period before the last day of tenancy; unless evicting, landlord must give the same notice the tenant must give. (SD Attorney General Consumer Protection, Landlord and Tenant fast facts; source)
